description: An UPDATE or DELETE with an ALIASED target must bind that alias for correlated subqueries in its WHERE, so UPDATE tgt t ... WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM src s WHERE t.k = s.k) correlates PER TARGET ROW. Without the alias binding the alias-qualified OUTER reference fell back to the INNER table's same-named column, which turned the correlation into a tautology: EXISTS then matched every row and NOT EXISTS none, so the disappeared-row-marking idiom updated nothing at all. Pinned four ways - the NOT EXISTS marking idiom, a plain correlated EXISTS, the two combined so only one row qualifies, and the same correlation under DELETE. Converted 1:1 from query/UpdateDeleteCorrelatedWhereTest (now retired); the Java collected the target's states into a Java HashMap keyed by k/sid, so the converted tests read the same key expression back as an ordered row set.

CREATE TABLE feed (k VARCHAR, sid VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO tracked VALUES ('a','s1','CURRENT'), ('a','s2','CURRENT'), ('b','s9','CURRENT')
INSERT INTO feed VALUES ('a','s1')
UPDATE tracked t SET t.st = 'DELETED' WHERE t.st != 'DELETED' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM feed s WHERE t.k = s.k AND t.sid = s.sid)
SELECT k || '/' || sid AS id, st FROM tracked ORDER BY id
